items.title: Changing lanes: mirror, signal, glance
items.simple: Before you change lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors. Turn on your signal. Look for other cars moving into the same lane. Then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
items.official: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic approaching you from behind. Then, use your turn signal to let other drivers know you plan to change lanes. Check for other drivers who also may be moving into the same lane. Just before you begin moving into the other lane, quickly glance over your shoulder and check for any vehicles that may be in your blind spot.
items.mnemonic: Mirror, signal, shoulder. Then move.

items.title: Slower traffic keeps right
items.simple: On a highway with many lanes, are you slower than the cars around you? Stay in the right lane. The left lane is for passing only. Don't ride along in it.
items.official: When driving on a multi-lane highway, stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than the traffic around you. The left lane is for passing only. When passing, use the left lane and avoid cruising.
items.mnemonic: Slow? Stay right. Left lane is for passing, not cruising.

items.title: Passing: check, signal, return
items.simple: Before you pass, check ahead, behind and your blind spot. Signal. Then speed up to pass. When you see the passed car's front in your rearview mirror, move back right.
items.official: Check the traffic ahead of you, behind you and in your blind spot before you attempt to pass. Signal and then accelerate to pass. Return to the right lane as soon as you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
items.mnemonic: See its front in your mirror, then move back.

items.title: No speeding while passing
items.simple: Never go over the speed limit, even to pass another car. Speeding to pass is against the law.
items.official: It is against the law to exceed the speed limit as you pass.
items.mnemonic: Passing is never a reason to speed.

items.title: Finish passing before the zone
items.simple: Finish your pass before you reach a No Passing zone. Still in the left lane when the zone starts? Then you are breaking the law.
items.official: Complete the pass before you reach a No Passing zone. If you're still in the left lane when you reach the zone, you're breaking the law.
items.mnemonic: See the pennant? Your pass must already be done.

items.title: Passing on the right
items.simple: Is the car ahead signaling and turning left? Then you may pass it on the right. Be careful. It may block your view. Never use the shoulder or leave the pavement to pass.
items.official: You may pass on the right if the vehicle you are passing has signaled and is making a left turn. Be cautious because the vehicle you are passing may be blocking your view or blocking the view of other drivers. You may not pass on the right if you must drive off the pavement or main portion of the roadway. Passing is unlawful and unsafe off the pavement or on the shoulder of the road.
items.mnemonic: Left-turner ahead? Pass on the right. Never on the shoulder.

items.title: 3 feet to pass a bike
items.simple: When you come up to a bike or moped, slow down. Pass at least 3 feet to its left. If your lane is too narrow for 3 feet, change lanes to pass.
items.official: When approaching or passing a person riding a bicycle, moped, or power-assisted bicycle or other device, reduce speed and pass at least three feet to the left. If the lane is not wide enough to allow for a three-foot clearance, the motorist must change lanes to pass safely.
items.mnemonic: Bike gets a yardstick: 3 feet.

items.title: Being passed: don't speed up
items.simple: When another car is passing you, do not speed up. Keep a steady speed or slow down.
items.official: When being passed, don't speed up. Maintain a steady speed or slow down.
items.mnemonic: Being passed? Let them go.

items.title: No passing on hills or curves
items.simple: Do not pass on hills or curves. Do not pass at intersections or railroad crossings. It is against the law and unsafe. This rule does not count when 2 or more lanes go your way.
items.official: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, at intersections or railroad crossings, except on roads with two or more lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
items.mnemonic: Hills, curves, crossroads, railroads: no passing.

items.title: Never pass a stopped school bus
items.simple: Never pass a school bus stopped to let riders on or off. This is true on public and private roads. Public road split by a barrier or unpaved median? Then you may go on.
items.official: Passing is unlawful and unsafe when a school bus is stopped to load or unload passengers on a public road (unless a physical barrier or unpaved median separates traffic going in either direction) or on a private road.

items.title: Solid line on left: no passing
items.simple: Is there a solid line on the left side of your lane? Then do not pass. Passing there is against the law and unsafe.
items.official: Passing is unlawful and unsafe when a solid line marks the left side of your lane.
items.mnemonic: Solid line on your side = stay in your lane.

items.title: No passing at a crosswalk
items.simple: Is the car ahead of you stopped at a crosswalk? Or the car in the next lane? Do not pass it. A person may be crossing where you can't see.
items.official: Passing is unlawful and unsafe when approaching a crosswalk and the vehicle ahead of you or the lane next to you is stopped. Passing at a crosswalk is illegal. You may not see pedestrians crossing the road in front of other vehicles.
items.mnemonic: Stopped car at a crosswalk? A walker may be hidden. Don't pass.

items.title: Over-correcting and running off road
items.simple: Turning the wheel too sharply can make the back of the car slide. If you drift off the road, don't panic. Slow down gradually. Look where you want to go. Steer back slowly.
items.official: Over-correcting occurs when the driver turns the steering wheel more sharply than expected, causing the rear wheels of the vehicle to slide toward the outside of the turn. Reduce speed and use extra caution while driving on curved roads. If you veer off the road, curved or straight, do not panic. Gradually reduce your speed, look in the direction you want to go, slowly steer back onto the roadway.
items.mnemonic: Off the road? Ease off, look, steer back slow.

items.title: Facing left turns: passenger sides
items.simple: Two cars face each other and both turn left. Each car turns in front of the other. Your passenger side passes their passenger side.
items.official: When two vehicles are approaching each other and signaling to turn left, both vehicles should turn in front of each other so that the passenger sides of the vehicles are beside each other.
items.mnemonic: Both turning left? Passenger side to passenger side.

items.title: U-turns: where and how
items.simple: Check for No U-Turn or No Left Turn signs first. In cities, towns and business districts, U-turn only at an intersection. Never U-turn on a highway. Signal left, stop, yield, then go into the right-hand lane.
items.official: Before you make a U-turn, check for No U-Turn or No Left Turn signs. In business districts, cities and towns, U-turns are allowed only at intersections. Never make a U-turn on a highway. When making a U-turn, turn on your left-turn signal, stop, and yield for approaching traffic. When the way is clear, proceed into the outside or right hand lane traveling in the opposite direction.
items.mnemonic: Town U-turn? Only at the corner. Highway U-turn? Never.

items.title: Turn signals are the law
items.simple: You must signal before you change lanes, turn, or enter or leave a highway. It is the law. Signal even if no one is around. After the turn, make sure the signal turns off.
items.official: When you plan to change lanes, turn, or enter or exit a highway, first give the proper turn signal. Using your turn signal is required by law. Use turn signals or hand signals even if no other traffic is on the road. After you complete the turn or lane change, be sure the turn signal stops flashing.
items.mnemonic: Turn, change, enter, exit: signal every time.

items.title: Signal 100 feet ahead
items.simple: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. That is 100 feet before the turn.
items.official: When you plan to turn, signal three or four seconds, 100 feet, ahead of your turn.
items.mnemonic: Signal early: 3-4 seconds, 100 feet.

items.title: Hand signal: left turn
items.simple: To signal a left turn by hand, stick your left arm straight out the window.
items.official: Left Turn: left hand and arm pointing straight out.
items.mnemonic: Straight out points left, the way you will go.

items.title: Hand signal: right turn
items.simple: To signal a right turn by hand, put your left arm out the window. Bend it so your hand points up.
items.official: Right Turn: left hand and arm pointing upward.
items.mnemonic: Right = Raised.

items.title: Hand signal: slow or stop
items.simple: To signal slow or stop by hand, put your left arm out the window. Bend it so your hand points down.
items.official: Slow or Stop: left hand and arm pointing downward.
items.mnemonic: Arm down = slowing down.

items.title: Right turn: right lane to curb
items.simple: To turn right, be in the lane farthest right. Signal. Look left and right for people and cars. Brake smoothly. At a red light or stop sign, stop fully first. Turn into the lane closest to the curb.
items.official: To make a right turn you should be in the lane furthest to the right. Signal at least three or four seconds, 100 feet, ahead of the turn. Look to your left and right to check the intersection for pedestrians and traffic. Brake smoothly before and during the turn. If there is a red traffic light or a stop sign, come to a complete stop before you make the turn. Turn into the lane closest to the curb unless pavement markings lead you otherwise.
items.mnemonic: Right lane in, curb lane out.

items.title: Left turn: start and end left
items.simple: To turn left, be in the lane farthest left. Turn into the leftmost lane of the new road. Several left-turn lanes? Pick the one that best fits where you go next.
items.official: To make a left turn you should be in the furthest left lane possible, turning into the leftmost lane on the intersecting road, unless pavement markings lead you otherwise; or, unless multiple left turn lanes are provided. If multiple left turn lanes are provided, you should choose the lane that will best serve your need once you enter the intersecting road.
items.mnemonic: Left lane in, left lane out.

items.title: Left turn: wheels straight
items.simple: While you wait to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight. If someone hits you from behind, you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic. Yield to cars, bikes and people coming toward you.
items.official: Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead until you are actually going to make the left turn. This prevents you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if another vehicle crashes into you from behind. When the way is clear, make the left turn, yield to any vehicles (including bicycles and pedestrians) approaching from the opposite direction.
items.mnemonic: Waiting to turn? Wheels stay straight.

items.title: Set mirrors before you drive
items.simple: Set your mirrors before you drive. The inside mirror should show the whole back window. Set each side mirror so you can barely see the side of your car.
items.official: Blind spots are danger areas where vehicles around you cannot be easily seen. Before driving, adjust your vehicle's mirrors. Make sure the inside rear view mirror frames the entire back window. Adjust both side mirrors so you can barely see the sides of your vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Inside: whole back window. Sides: barely see your car.

items.title: Don't ride in blind spots
items.simple: Don't drive in another driver's blind spot. It is as dangerous as not checking your own. Speed up or drop back so you are not stuck there.
items.official: Avoid driving in someone else's blind spot. This can be just as dangerous as not checking your own blind spot. Speed up or drop back; but, don't stay in the other driver's blind spot.
items.mnemonic: Don't hang out beside them. Speed up or drop back.

items.title: Backing up: turn and look
items.simple: Mirrors do not show everything behind you. To back up, turn your body and head to the right. Look out the back window. Back up slowly. Glance quickly to each side for people and cars.
items.official: The most common mistake that drivers make when backing up is failing to look both ways behind them. Mirrors do not give you a full view. To see as much as possible, turn your body and head to the right and look out through the rear window. Back up slowly and check for pedestrians and approaching traffic by glancing quickly to either side.
items.mnemonic: Backing up? Turn around and look back.

items.title: Park within 1 foot of curb
items.simple: Park as far from traffic as you can. Next to a curb, park no more than 1 foot away. On a two-way street, park on the right side. On a one-way street, either side is OK.
items.official: When parking on a public road, move as far from traffic as possible. If you park on a shoulder, pull over as far on the shoulder as possible. If you park next to a curb, pull close to it. You may not park more than one foot from the curb. On a two-way street, park on the right side of the road. On a one-way road, park on either side.
items.mnemonic: One foot from the curb, right side of a two-way street.

items.title: Uphill with curb: wheels left
items.simple: Parking uphill next to a curb? Turn your front wheels to the left, away from the curb. This keeps your car from rolling into the street.
items.official: Parking on a hill with a curb: turn the front wheels of your vehicle to prevent it from rolling into the street. Parking uphill with curb: turn front wheels left.
items.mnemonic: Up, up and away: uphill, turn away from the curb.

items.title: Downhill with curb: wheels right
items.simple: Parking downhill next to a curb? Turn your front wheels to the right, toward the curb. This keeps your car from rolling into the street.
items.official: Parking on a hill with a curb: turn the front wheels of your vehicle to prevent it from rolling into the street. Parking downhill with curb: turn front wheels right.
items.mnemonic: Downhill? Wheels go down to the curb.

items.title: Hill, no curb: wheels right
items.simple: Parking on a hill with no curb? Uphill or downhill, turn your front wheels to the right. If the car rolls, the back will roll away from traffic.
items.official: Without a curb: turn the front wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, the rear of the vehicle will roll away from traffic. Parking uphill or downhill with no curb: turn front wheels right.
items.mnemonic: No curb? Always turn right.

items.title: Look before opening your door
items.simple: When you get out of your car, watch for traffic. Look for cars, bikes and people walking before you open your door.
items.official: Be aware of other traffic when exiting your vehicle. Look for other cars, bicyclists, and pedestrians before opening the door.
items.mnemonic: Look, then open.

items.title: 15 feet: hydrant, fire station
items.simple: Park at least 15 feet away from a fire hydrant. Also stay 15 feet from the entrance of a fire, ambulance or rescue squad station.
items.official: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, or within 15 feet of the entrance to a fire, ambulance or rescue squad station.
items.mnemonic: Hydrant 15, corner 20, train 50, fire trucks 500.

items.title: 20 feet from an intersection
items.simple: When you park, stay at least 20 feet back from an intersection.
items.official: You may not park within 20 feet of an intersection.
items.mnemonic: Hydrant 15, corner 20, train 50, fire trucks 500.

items.title: 500 feet from fire trucks
items.simple: Are fire trucks or fire equipment stopped to answer an alarm? Park at least 500 feet away from them.
items.official: You may not park within 500 feet of where fire trucks or equipment are stopped answering an alarm.
items.mnemonic: Hydrant 15, corner 20, train 50, fire trucks 500.

items.title: 50 feet from railroad crossing
items.simple: Park at least 50 feet away from a railroad crossing.
items.official: You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
items.mnemonic: Hydrant 15, corner 20, train 50, fire trucks 500.

items.title: Places you may never park
items.simple: Never park beside a parked car. Or on a crosswalk or sidewalk. Or in front of a driveway. No parking at yellow curbs, No Parking signs or bike lanes. Stay out of disabled spaces and their striped aisles.
items.official: You may not park: beside another parked vehicle (double parking); on crosswalks or sidewalks; in front of driveways; within areas where parking is prohibited by curbs painted yellow or No Parking signs; in a parking space reserved for disabled persons; in striped access aisles adjacent to a parking space reserved for disabled persons; on the hard surface of a road when no curb is present; in a bike lane; in such a way that you block or create a hazard for other vehicles in a designated traffic lane.

items.title: Disabled space and its aisle
items.simple: Do not park in a space saved for disabled persons. Also do not park in the striped aisle next to it. People need that space to get in and out.
items.official: You may not park: in a parking space reserved for disabled persons; in striped access aisles adjacent to a parking space reserved for disabled persons.
items.mnemonic: Stripes next to the disabled space are not a parking spot.

items.title: No curb: get off the pavement
items.simple: Park as far from traffic as you can. If there is no curb, do not park on the hard road surface. Pull as far onto the shoulder as you can. Never block a traffic lane.
items.official: When parking on a public road, move as far from traffic as possible. If you park on a shoulder, pull over as far on the shoulder as possible. You may not park: on the hard surface of a road when no curb is present; in such a way that you block or create a hazard for other vehicles in a designated traffic lane.
items.mnemonic: No curb? Wheels off the pavement.

events.prompt: Curvy road ahead!

events.prompt: Using turn signals is:

events.missLine: Signal 3 to 4 seconds, 100 feet, before your turn.

events.prompt: Signal a turn how many seconds ahead?
events.missLine: Signal 3 to 4 seconds before your turn.

events.prompt: Right turn coming up. Signal how far ahead?
events.missLine: Signal at least 100 feet before the turn.

events.prompt: This hand signal means what?
events.missLine: Left arm straight out means a left turn.

events.prompt: How do you signal a left turn by hand?
events.missLine: For a left turn, hold your left arm straight out.

events.prompt: Your left arm points straight out. You plan to:
events.missLine: Left arm straight out means you will turn left.

events.prompt: The driver ahead shows this. They will:
events.missLine: Left arm bent up means a right turn.

events.prompt: Hand signal for a right turn?
events.missLine: For a right turn, point your left arm upward.

events.missLine: Left arm bent down means slow or stop.

events.prompt: Signaling a stop by hand. Arm points:
events.missLine: To signal slow or stop, point your left arm downward.

events.prompt: Driver ahead shows this hand signal.
events.missLine: Arm pointing down means the driver ahead will slow or stop.

events.prompt: Right turn at a stop sign.
events.missLine: At a stop sign, stop completely before you turn right.

events.prompt: Turning right. Which lane do you end in?
events.missLine: After a right turn, enter the lane closest to the curb.

events.prompt: To turn right, start in which lane?
events.missLine: Make a right turn from the lane furthest to the right.

events.prompt: Red light. You want to turn right.
events.missLine: At a red light, stop completely before you turn right.

events.prompt: To turn left, start in which lane?
events.missLine: Make a left turn from the furthest left lane possible.

events.prompt: Turning left. Which lane do you enter?
events.missLine: Turn into the leftmost lane of the new road.

events.prompt: Waiting to turn left. Your wheels point:
events.missLine: Keep front wheels straight until you actually turn left.

events.prompt: Why keep wheels straight while waiting?
events.missLine: Straight wheels keep you out of oncoming traffic if you are hit from behind.

events.prompt: Turning left. People in the crosswalk.
events.missLine: When you turn, yield and let people in the crosswalk cross first.

events.prompt: Your inside mirror should frame what?
events.missLine: The inside mirror should frame the entire back window.

events.prompt: Side mirrors set right. How much of your car?
events.missLine: Set side mirrors so you can barely see the sides of your car.

events.prompt: When do you adjust your mirrors?
events.missLine: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving.

events.prompt: You're in a car's blind spot. Do what?
events.missLine: Speed up or drop back so you never stay in another driver's blind spot.

events.prompt: Driving in someone's blind spot is:
events.missLine: Riding in another driver's blind spot is dangerous.

events.prompt: Backing up. Where do you look?
events.missLine: Turn your body and head right and look out the rear window.

events.prompt: Most common backing mistake?

events.prompt: How fast should you back up?

events.prompt: Parked at a curb. How far away, at most?
events.missLine: You may not park more than 1 foot from the curb.

events.prompt: Parking on a two-way street. Which side?
events.missLine: On a two-way street, park on the right side.

events.prompt: Parking on a one-way street. Which side?
events.missLine: On a one-way road, you may park on either side.

events.prompt: Uphill with a curb. Turn wheels which way?
events.missLine: Uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels left.

events.prompt: Uphill at a curb. Wheels point:
events.missLine: Uphill with a curb, turn wheels away from the curb.

events.prompt: Downhill with a curb. Turn wheels which way?
events.missLine: Downhill with a curb, turn your front wheels right.

events.prompt: Downhill at a curb. Wheels point:
events.missLine: Downhill with a curb, turn wheels toward the curb.

events.prompt: Hill with no curb. Turn wheels which way?
events.missLine: With no curb, turn your front wheels right, uphill or downhill.

events.prompt: No curb, parked uphill. Wheels point:
events.missLine: Uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels right.

events.prompt: Why turn wheels right with no curb?
events.missLine: Turned right, the car's rear rolls away from traffic.

events.prompt: Parked on the street. Before you open the door:
events.missLine: Look for cars, bicyclists and pedestrians before opening the door.

events.prompt: Bike coming as you open your door. Do what?
events.missLine: Check for bicyclists before you open your door.

events.prompt: Closest you may park to a fire hydrant?

events.prompt: Fire station entrance. Park at least how far away?
events.missLine: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire station entrance.

events.prompt: Rescue squad entrance. Park no closer than:
events.missLine: Stay 15 feet from a fire, ambulance or rescue squad entrance.

events.prompt: Closest you may park to an intersection?

events.prompt: Parking near a corner. Stay back how far?

events.prompt: Fire trucks at an alarm. Park no closer than:

events.prompt: Fire engines answering an alarm. Park how far away?
events.missLine: Stay 500 feet from fire trucks stopped at an alarm.

events.prompt: Closest you may park to a railroad crossing?
events.missLine: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.

events.prompt: Parking near train tracks. Stay back:
events.missLine: Park at least 50 feet from a railroad crossing.

events.prompt: Can you park in front of a driveway?
events.missLine: You may not park in front of a driveway.

events.prompt: Yellow curb. Can you park here?
events.missLine: You may not park where curbs are painted yellow.

events.prompt: Parking beside a parked car is called:
events.missLine: Double parking, beside another parked car, is not allowed.

events.prompt: Can you park in a bike lane?
events.missLine: You may not park in a bike lane.

events.prompt: Signal is on. Who else may move into that lane?
events.missLine: Check for other drivers who also may be moving into the same lane.

events.prompt: Turning the wheel too sharply can make what slide?

events.prompt: Winding road in the rain.
